reviews.author: Ke'Liana Adams
reviews.text: Very fun twisty and turny drive, including 2 bridges-- one 2 lane and one single lane, across each portion of the rivers that created the awesomeness that is the Cove ❤️👌

reviews.author: Sampor Burke
reviews.text: Beautiful little park with great views and a relaxing atmosphere. The playground was clean and fun for kids, and there were plenty of picnic areas to sit and enjoy the scenery. It’s also very dog-friendly with lots of space to walk. Restrooms were decent and easy to access. Overall a peaceful spot for families, pets, or just getting outside for a bit.

reviews.author: Teresa Melville
reviews.text: Went in the off season, but quickly learned the view puts this place always in season.

reviews.author: Gary Currie
reviews.text:
We had never been to this gem.
It was just a drive through to check it out, but wow, what an amazing surprise.
Another Oregon State Park that is truly breathtaking.
Looks like tons of great camping, boating,  swimming when the algae is gone, and just chilling.
We are definitely going back to camp.
Don't let this beauty not be visited.
It's 4 stars because until I camp.

reviews.author: Cheri Wright
reviews.text: We did not stay here but did a drive thru around the whole thing. Campgrounds are dry and nothing fancy. But have hook ups in some spots. The lake is huge. It was very windy when we went and water was rough. Water was very green so not sure if that's anything to worry about. Very popular with Boaters. Beautiful canyon views.

reviews.author: Joanne L
reviews.text: Amazing love it have been here the last 4 years will continue to go every year after my family loves it or friends love it it is our favorite thing to do every summer

This is an incredible Oregon park that is worth the quick, free stop. I had visited years ago, so I knew when I was back in the area with my wife and friends, I had to show them. They were amazed and there was no one around, so we had the views to ourselves.
We had an amazing time renting a boat from the Marina! Reasonable price, friendly service. Great explanation of the lake, where to fish and what to see.

When I inquired about rentals at the Marina, the really supportive and knowledgeable staff stated that CP was central Oregon's best kept secret ... I agree. A large group rented and shared 2 pontoon boats for the day. Just a great experience working with the staff. Each group had a 4 hour pontoon rental. We all had a fantastic relaxing experience on the boat getting a chance to see all 3 arms of the canyon. It was recommended that we visit on a Wednesday to avoid crowds and they were correct. About $300 +gas for the day ... great deal if you share the cost with a group.
Clean facilities. Full hookups. Roomy sites. We love The Cove. Hosts and rangers are very nice, friendly and helpful

A beautiful place. The night sky is AMAZING. We stayed in Loop B, B21. It is a very large tent site. It has a sandy area by the vehicle pad site, then walk up through the boulders and there is a campfire ring, and walk up further and a grassy area for your tent with a picnic table. It was again surprisingly large! you can't tell that from the photo when reserving the site. If you want to be close to restrooms I suggest reserving anything after B32. Also, B32 is right next to the dumpster, which has a lot of lizards and squirrels next to it. B 21 and the sites next to them are all spacious on that side, it does back up to the state park road, so at night when everyone comes back to the campsite you can hear traffic, but it wasn't disturbing. We noticed most people came back to camp around 6 pm and would stay up until midnight at least. There is a hill and a walk if you reserve anything before B32 for restrooms/showers and the play area. The bathrooms have a shower area, very small 3 shower stalls, and 1 of the women's showers was broken, it can get very busy. The bathroom was extremely hot. The park staff and volunteers drive by continuously through the day ( not sure if that was because it was a holiday weekend or not), but we saw the sheriff many many times driving around, and even stopped to talk a bit. We stayed July 2-4 2021. It was HOT in the 90's-100 degrees. It was unbearable during the day, and quickly realized why everyone was out of the campsite during the day and came back at night. If you want to go use the DAY use area's get there early morning, or there won't be parking AT ALL. We were lucky to drive to the first day-use area when entering the park, the ones closest to ABC campsites were full all day. We were lucky enough to get a parking spot and able to find a shaded area close to the restrooms to get into the swimming area. That too was PACKED, and everyone brought their easy-ups, ( so smart!), there are plenty of picnic tables, if you are able to get one. Everyone was respectful, but in order to get into the water, you do have to go through areas of the shoreline that preoccupied. This was our first trip to this state park, and we will go again, now we have more knowledge of what to expect and what to do differently next time. The night skies is what I look forward to the most.

Stopped here for a couple days. The first day was very HOT. The next days were very nice. The park has very good RV camping spots with full hookups. The restrooms are very clean and showers are great. Even though there were lots of children around playing etc., they all were very well behaved. This was our first visit and we are planning on returning. The only negative is the lack of near by ice. There is a small store with several ice storage boxes, but there are only open Friday, Saturday and Sunday for a couple hours each day. If you need ice any other day, you have to go to the marina or to town. The store is run by a third party.

Gorgeous High Desert with Jaw-Dropping Views, Lake and Hiking! Warning: gets scorching-hot in high summer! Great for anyone who loves doing things on the water but be advised, lots of noise from boats when it's busy! Lovely hiking but limited: there are really only two in total: if you're camping at Deschutes, you can make a lovely 4.5-mile daily walk which is almost all on trails, and it's so nice I'd return to this park just to be able to go on this walk again! There is also the well-known Tamalau trail which goes a mile up to the top of the canyon and then for miles on a loop around the mesa--the complete walk is 7 miles plus the distance to your campsite. The hike to the top is only recommended when it's cool, so early morning or a day that's not hot. It's not particularly hard but it's exposed and murderously hot when it's a warm day. (In other words, "hotter than Satan's XXXXXXX!!") Once you get to the top, it's all exposed too--this hike comes with posted warnings for overheating and they are not kidding! We've done it twice--once when it was too hot and the other time when it was cool and overcast--perfect! If you want any more hiking, there is another short hike from the campground across the canyon, and one other I believe, but this place is pretty devoid of trails, so keep that in mind. Biking: good luck on that unless you like roads and sharing them with construction vehicles hell-bent on getting from Point A to Point B. Short rides around the campground loops are very nice though, but don't expect miles of trails--they aren't there and the hiking trails are not suitable for bikes. Fishing is fantastic here, and you can rent a boat from the marina to go to the two "scum-lines", where the Crooked and Deschutes rivers meet the lake--this mixing water attracts fish like crazy and we've caught many delicious trout there! Water Sport Heaven! Anyone who loves boating, jet-skiing and the like will have a fabulous time here, it's a total mecca. Campsites: this campground accommodates everyone and include primitive campsites to spaces for 60-foot+ RVs like our truck and 5th wheel, and they have plenty of full hookups too. Clean bathrooms, wonderfully kept grounds, this place is a total winner! Cell Phone and Internet junkies: BE ADVISED, there is NO CONNECTIVITY! Even with our Wii-Boost and 20-foot antenna, there was nothing. The rare person with ATT can get a signal but Verizon users will be out of luck. Will you be staying at The Cove Palisades? If you are, would you please help keep the ground squirrels safe? There is a dumpster in Loop A for the tent campers and ground squirrels climb in but they can't get out. Which means they die of heat prostration and thirst. The easy solution is to put a branch in the corner so they can climb out, which is what we did. But when I told rangers about the pile of dead squirrels I'd found and the desperate squirrels trying to escape, they nodded and said it was horrible and they'd be right on it, but they did nothing. The next time I checked, I was livid to discover I'd been lied to. I put a branch in and an hour later the trapped ones had climbed out. If you find this is still an issue, would you please complain to the rangers and make a stink? If enough people make waves, they'll have to fix this situation. And all it takes is a branch or a ladder so they can climb out. It's not right. I've often said the worst way to die is in a fire, being burned to death. That is the hell these poor squirrels are dealing with. It really needs to stop, the squirrels were here first.

I usually camp at dispersed camping sites and rarely RV camp in RV parks. My experience at Cove Palisades State Park was memorable for all the right reasons. Checking out the park on the website and seeing over 175 sites I was not concerned about finding one available. What a surprise! I stopped at the upper campground and received some of the best guest service ever. Wish I had written names down. I was told there were two sites available. After she had all the info in the computer I mentioned hiking and she said oh we should see if they have anything available in the lower area. She called and asked them to hold the very last site available for us. What great service. Arriving at the kiosk at the lower site we were once again greeted with a huge smile, welcome and wealth of information about the park. We were provided hiking brochures, great map of the park and told to come back if the site did not suite us. They would check to see if anyone had checked out early. The park in itself is amazingly beautiful. We are a senior couple and found it joyful to see so many young families with small children. A huge playground, tether ball, volleyball, horseshoes, small store, and shower/bath rooms made it the most family friendly park I have ever visited. Quiet time was 10 pm and at exactly that time a hush came over the entire park. It was as if someone sprinkled magic dust over the park and everyone went to sleep. A must do is to hike the Tam-a-la'u Trail. A grueling steep climb for the 1st mile is not for wimps to be sure. However, once on top of the ridge you are gifted with a view one can't describe in words. Once at the top a 3.5 mile loop around the ridge is breathtaking. No adjectives worthy enough to describe it. I must admit that on one of my rest stops one the way up a woman packing a baby around 9 months old passed me on the trail so it must not be to wimpy! I saw signs mentioning houseboat rentals not sure of the cost. The boating and swimming must be excellent from all the towels I saw hanging on clothes lines at campsites and boats parked and in the lake. My full service site with sewer was $30 per night. I really appreciated the wonderful recycling centers easily located around the park. On a park walk I noticed several recycling areas and shower buildings. There are also small buildings with sinks for cleaning fish. Oh and a place for tent campers to wash their camp dishes. Truly if your thinking of taking your family camping give this park a chance!

We'd never stayed at this park before. I was amazed at its cleanliness, considering how many people were there. It is very heavily used, mostly by boaters, who take their boats onto the Crooked River. I have seldom seen a better maintained or appointed state park. There are lots of sites, things for kids to do, and grass and trees throughout. While there was no privacy between sites, each site had water and electricity, grass and some shade trees. Sites are small. The parking pad for your camper isn't going to accommodate your tow vehicle,so they let people park their boat trailers on the grass. That makes for some difficult manuevering when you're trying to get a big 5th wheel/RV into the spot and your across the road neighbor has left his boat trailer half way into the road. I am really surprised that the rangers don't insist on people using the overflow parking lot, which is very large and was hardly used. There is a substantial recycling spot, a garbage compactor and a very clean and useable dump station. This park has it all! The bathrooms (flush toilets and free showers) were clean. The Park is separated into into three sections, one is across the river (reached by a rather narrow bridge). The River and the geological Palisades are incredible. While we were there we saw turkey vultures soaring past the rainbowed waterfall. It was an incredible sight. So are the rocks themselves. You can see where columnar basalt has been covered with volcanic ashfall sometime in the past. The Palisades are worth the trip all on it's own. Considering how many people were in the campground, everyone seemed to honor the quiet time policy as it was silent as a tomb after dark. This is the first park I've ever seen that had an Off Leash Dog Area. It was well used and well supplied with poopy bags....and still some folks let their dog poop elsewhere in the park, wherever the mood took it. They always pretend to not know what the dog at the end of the leash is doing, do not pick up the poop and walk off unconcernedly, without a lick of shame. Shame on them. This is why I think dogs should not be allowed in campgrounds..but that will never happen. I know it. But otherwise, this campground is very, very good and I recommend it.

reviews.author: PKBucketListTrip
reviews.text: Loved the Or State Cove Palisades state park campground - facilities here are super clean A++++ clean! The lake is fun for folks of all ages. Tubing, paddle boarding, kayaking, etc, etc. Dry heat during day and cools down beautifully at night - cool enough to enjoy a campfire. Stars at night are magnificent for viewing. Cove Palisades - Cove named for the swimming area and Palisades for the volcanic vertical rocks. Pictures cannot capture the magnitude or colors of these rocks, nor do they capture the beauty, IMO. Not too far from Smith Rock, Bend, etc, if you want to venture out during your stay.

reviews.author: YellowRaven
reviews.text: This is primarily an SUV camp ground, lots and lots of sites. But nestled away just south of the boat moorage area are 3 deluxe cabins (with showers and a kitchen. They all face the lake, there is a great communal fire pit next to the lake. The cabins are in a very private location being behind a small hill with tree cover. Getting one is a matter of playing the game of finding a reservation, they allow you to book 9 months in advance. Good spot, you just have to plan your trip ahead of time. Beautiful area.

reviews.author: Debbie M.
reviews.text: There are 2 campgrounds in The Cove Palisades; Crooked River Campground, which is the upper or rim campground, and Deschutes Campground, which is the lower campground at Lake Billy Chinook level, another 5 miles drive down into the canyon past the upper campground. This review is for Deschutes Campground. We stayed at Deshutes a week with our travel trailer in loop A in mid May. We would stay here again. I would not want to stay here during wildfire season due to the smoke and low visibility (personal preference), plus I'm not crazy about hot weather and it would certainly be hot in the high desert in summer as well as crowded which is also not my thing. Every time you come and go from this campsite, you have a 5 mile drive in or out of this canyon. I have Republic Wireless on Sprint and had no signal within the canyon but did at the top. Husband has Cricket on AT&T and had a signal in the canyon. Our antenna did not pick up any TV channels so download some Netflix to your device before coming here, or maybe have a better antenna than we do if you desire to watch anything. The hosts take great care of the grounds. I do not know the condition of the bathrooms but heard and read they were very clean as well. We spent most of our time away from the campground but the time we were there was pleasant and quiet. Our spot backed up to the road which was slightly above us so didn't really affect our view and there were some trees and shrubbery between us and the road. Occasionally a vehicle would go by that was quite loud which would be louder and more frequent in the busy season. We had a large gap between us and the campsite to our right as well as a view of the palisades on that side. We usually travel with our dog, but she recently passed away unfortunately so this trip was dogless, but I still view things from the eyes of a dog owner. They had a large, grassy, fenced-in dog park that would be a great respite as the campsites aren't that grassy, mostly dirt with some juniper trees, sage, and boulders. Watch for foxtails which we saw in spring, as well as rattlesnakes. We didn't see any rattlesnakes at the time we were there - a rainy, cool week in mid May. Because of all the rain, everything was still very green and all the wildflowers were in bloom. On a clear day you can see at least 6 mountain peaks from the top of the canyon. This is a great spot to explore Central Oregon. In fact, we need to go back because we didn't get to everything we wanted to do but we visited Richardson Rock Ranch, Smith Rock, Bend, Lava Lands, Oregon High Desert Museum, Glass Buttes, and more.

not really any privacy between sites; large rigs were playing music most of the night. but the surrounding area and drive into the park is SO stunning. would try staying here again though but maybe in a site on the outside of the loops

We drove to Cove Palisades and it was closed. We had paid for a reserved sight. We were not notified regarding the closure. Gate locked, cones across. We saw other people having to turn around also. Not happy
